agree.reason: The plain apology and the unchanged $540 price will reach this household, but nothing promises them money back if the boxes are thin again, which was their main grievance, so a wary reader may still hold off.

honest.reason: The facts and figures are accurate, including that the nets cover only tomatoes and peppers, but 'you'll hear from me quickly and you'll get the whole story' is a vague promise the writer was never given in those words.

works_the_facts.reason: Setting the $31,000 spend beside the unchanged $540 price works well, but the email leaves out the survey result that 29 of 41 people who answered would return if bad weeks were handled better, and it calculates nothing new.

right_comparison.reason: It says the price is the same as last year, but it never sets rejoining against the household's real alternative, and it doesn't make clear that the nets leave the greens exposed.

qualification.reason: 'I can't promise good weather' is a hedge the reader can't check, and the email skips the concrete commitment that was available: a credit for any week weather cuts a box by more than a third, plus a weekly Thursday email.

objections.reason: The apology deals with the silence after the hail, but the main objection, 'what if the boxes are thin again and I get no credit?', goes unanswered, because the two-week pause credit is a different thing.

fit.reason: It is an email of under 200 words, as asked, but it leaves [Name], [Your name] and [Farm name] as placeholders even though the details were known, and it doesn't give the sign-up link on the website.
